blocks.title: The big idea
blocks.body: AI can propose and modify code, but fluent output is not ownership or evidence. Define the result, bound each change, inspect reality and keep the human responsible for understanding, integration and release.

blocks.title: Before coding
items: User story: who needs what, and why
Scope: included work and explicit non-goals
Data: information and important definitions
Edges: repeated actions, empty values and failures
Acceptance criteria: observable outcomes to check

blocks.title: Reviewable changes
items: Checkpoint the intended current Git state
Match batch size to risk and review capacity
Keep unrelated rewrites out of the change
Read every relevant part of the actual diff
Accept only code you can explain

blocks.title: Evidence loop
items: Reproduce with starting state and exact actions
Record expected and actual results
Preserve the full error and its location
Reduce the case while retaining the failure
Test one hypothesis and rerun the same case
Revert a change unsupported by the evidence

blocks.title: Useful checks
items: Behavior: an ordinary required outcome
Boundary: edges and transitions between states
Failure: rejected input or unavailable resources
Regression: the conditions of a previous bug
Run tests and inspect actual output
Call tests unrun when execution did not happen

blocks.title: Final review
items: Keep secrets out of code, logs, prompts and Git
Revoke or rotate exposed secrets
Treat user, network, file and AI content as untrusted
Separate data from queries, commands and displays
Review permissions and sensitive-data handling

blocks.title: Dependency questions
items: Is this package necessary for the agreed outcome?
Can existing project or platform support do the job?
Are its source, maintenance and permissions acceptable?
Are its license terms compatible with project policy?
Can unused or duplicate dependencies be removed?

blocks.body: Tests provide evidence only for exercised cases. AI summaries do not replace diffs, execution or security review. The human owns secrets, permissions and the final decision.
